story: A master smith, one of three brothers, lived for a time with three swan maidens who were his lover and his brothers' lovers. After nine years the swan maidens departed; his brothers went searching for them and never returned. The smith's lover left him a ring before she departed, and he forged seven hundred copies of it. A king captured the smith while he slept, had him hamstrung so he could not walk, and imprisoned him on an island, forcing him to forge treasures for the king. The king gave the smith's ring to his own daughter and wore the smith's sword himself. In revenge, when the king's two sons secretly visited the smith's forge, he killed them, then made goblets from their skulls, jewels from their eyes, and a brooch from their teeth. He sent the goblets to the king, the jewels to the queen, and the brooch to the daughter. When the daughter brought her ring to him for mending, he tricked and seduced her, leaving her pregnant. He then crafted a winged garment and flew to the king's hall, where he revealed everything he had done: the murder of the sons, the jewelry made from their remains, and the seduction of the daughter. The grieving king could not stop him, for no archer or horseman could reach him in flight, and the smith escaped forever. The king summoned his daughter and asked if the smith's account was true; she confirmed it, saying she had been powerless against him because he was too strong for her.
